links.comparator_used: Prompt with no assigned persona (non-medical/no-persona baseline)
links.outcome: Task accuracy and calibration on clinical triage and patient-safety tasks
links.effect: Medical personas improve performance in critical care tasks, with gains of up to ~+20% in accuracy and calibration, but degrade performance in primary-care settings by comparable margins.
links.tradeoff: Degraded accuracy and calibration in primary-care settings; effects are context-dependent and non-monotonic; interaction style effects on risk propensity are highly model-dependent.
links.quote: We find systematic, context-dependent, and non-monotonic effects: Medical personas improve performance in critical care tasks, yielding gains of up to $\sim+20\%$ in accuracy and calibration, but degrade performance in primary-care settings by comparable margins.

design_hint: persona prompting (medical role and interaction style) as a prompt guardrail
